Opening

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON A · 2 MINUTES

Autumn Science: Build the Evidence Map

Learning objective

I can locate or create honest science evidence, explain what it shows and improve one response after a focused check.

Success looks like

  • Give a clear locator for an actual piece of evidence.
  • Connect a science claim to a relevant observation and a limit.
  • Label new evidence as new and keep a meaningful before/after response.

This is an evidence studio, not a memory test about missing worksheets. Use real work you can locate, or make a clearly labelled new response today.

Two separate lessons

A · Explore and explain · 40 minutes

B · Autumn Science: Explain, Check, Improve · 40 minutes

Stop after Lesson A. Lesson B has its own start and exit.

Point, speak, sign, move cards, draw, write or direct an adult. Choose one route; equivalent science evidence does not require a written conversion.

Arrival

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON A · 5 MINUTES

Four clues to start

Choose a route. Today’s responses decide the help you use. No previous worksheet is needed.

Supported · 4 questions

1. Findable evidence

Which is a useful locator: “somewhere” or “book page 6, table 1”?

Help beside the question
Point, choose or say. Another adult should be able to find it.

Answer guidance

Answer: Book page 6, table 1.

2. Missing work

Choose “not found yet” or “invent a page number”.

Help beside the question
Do not guess evidence.

Answer guidance

Answer: Not found yet.

3. New response

You explain a supplied card today. Is this new evidence or proof you wrote it last month?

Help beside the question
Point, choose or say. Separate today from an earlier record.

Answer guidance

Answer: New evidence.

4. Relevant reason

Which explains day/night: rotation or a recycling label?

Help beside the question
Point, choose or say. Match the science to the claim.

Answer guidance

Answer: Rotation.

I do

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON A · 7 MINUTES

Watch, predict, explain

Predict, model, explain

My claim is ___. My evidence is at ___. It supports the claim because ___. One limit is ___.

Make a prediction. Change one view, then use a label to explain what you notice.

Use a real page, file or named card. Do not invent a locator for missing work.

Worked explanation · reveal after thinking

Do not fabricate, backdate or silently substitute missing pupil evidence. The supplied cards are neutral teaching examples; pupils may respond to them now, labelled as new work. Automated choices, downloaded files and word count do not certify understanding or an award.

Local explainer · 32 seconds · silent with captions

Use instead of part of the demonstration. It never autoplays and needs no internet.

Full text / no-video alternative

00–08 seconds · Find an actual record
Use a real page, file or named card. Do not invent a locator for missing work.

08–16 seconds · Build the evidence link
Connect the claim, exact observation, science reason and an honest limit.

16–24 seconds · Make new evidence honestly
A response to today’s supplied card is new work, not a replacement dated as last month.

24–32 seconds · Explain and improve
Keep the first response. After one focused question, make a visible science improvement.

Read the card clues

Located table: A real file and table show three trials for each tested surface.

Today’s new answer: The response is labelled new and points to the supplied DN1 diagram.

Value with no unit: The record says 48 but does not identify the unit or measured quantity.

Claim only: The answer says “Earth rotates” but has not linked it to a light observation.

Invented old page: A page number was guessed because the earlier book is missing.

A click proves an award: A completed digital choice has not been judged against qualification criteria.

Would a small change help? · optional

You may ask for a clearer diagram, fewer cards at once, reading help or more thinking time. Tell your teacher, ask privately, point or pass. Your teacher will say what can change and check whether it helped. No extra sheet is needed.

Fresh case cards · no earlier work required

DN1 · day/night

Fixed light at LEFT. Earth-model marker at LEFT is lit; at RIGHT it is unlit. Explain the difference using rotation.

CL1 · warming

A greenhouse model includes an arrow carrying infrared energy out to space. Explain why “all energy is trapped forever” is wrong.

RR1 · rover

Invented values: smooth 48, 51, 49 cm; fabric 27, 29, 28 cm. Compare this setup without claiming every surface behaves the same.

SH1 · shape

Disc front = circular; disc at 90° = narrow. Ball outline remains circular at both angles. What difference does this support?

Honest recording

These are supplied teaching examples. Your response to one today is new evidence, not a backdated older task.

You do

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON A · 10 MINUTES

Use the evidence yourself

Supported · use one response mode

1. Locate

Choose one real record or one supplied case card.

Help: Use DN1, CL1, RR1 or SH1 if needed.

2. Explain

Point to one observation and finish a because sentence.

Help: An adult may scribe your words.

3. Identify a next step

Choose one missing unit, reason or locator to add.

Help: One accurate improvement is enough.

Standard · use one response mode

1. Locate

Map two claims to findable evidence, using honest labels.

Help: Real record / new response / not found yet.

2. Explain

Connect one claim to an exact observation and a science reason.

Help: Use a measurement or diagram position.

3. Identify a next step

Mark one useful evidence improvement without rewriting everything.

Help: Keep the first response.

Stretch · use one response mode

1. Locate

Select a balanced set of evidence and explain why each locator is sufficient.

Help: Do not infer missing work from a topic title.

2. Explain

Explain the strength and limits of two different evidence types.

Help: Model observations differ from independent physical evidence.

3. Identify a next step

Explain what further task could resolve one genuine uncertainty.

Help: New evidence should answer the actual gap.

Use the application model · an alternative to writing

Evidence-map decisions

Use the digital choices or the matching paper page. One response mode is enough.

Arrival, investigation, checking and refining total 32 minutes. Then review the evidence for four minutes and complete two exit checks in four minutes.

Supported · 4 questions

1. Source type

Is a model answer written by an adult automatically your own evidence?

Answer: No.

Why retain a first response before refining it?

Point, choose or say. Show the actual improvement.

Answer guidance

Answer: It lets us see which science idea was corrected or strengthened.

Workshop

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON B · 20 MINUTES

Gather and use evidence

Use only authorised pupil records; do not display another learner’s personal work. Provide the neutral examples for anyone without earlier sheets. Accept speaking, pointing or an adult-scribed record in the pupil’s own words; keep response modes equivalent.

4 min · Check source, locator and new/earlier status.
20 min · Explain a chosen record or supplied case. Keep the first response; have a partner or adult ask one evidence question.
2 min · Find the observation supporting the claim.
6 min · Improve the science and show the before/after change.
Neutral teaching caseExact observation to usePossible science link
DN1 · fixed-light modelLEFT lit; RIGHT unlitEarth rotates into/out of sunlight
CL1 · energy diagramAn outgoing infrared arrow remainsEnergy is not completely blocked
RR1 · supplied rover dataSmooth 48–51 cm; fabric 27–29 cmLonger smooth travel in this setup
SH1 · shape viewsDisc narrows at 90°; ball stays circularDifferent viewpoint patterns

Supported route

Use one supplied case card. Point to the observation, give a short explanation and improve one element with an adult’s question.

Standard route

Give claim, locator, observation, reason and limit. Keep a first and improved response and identify the science change.

Stretch route

Compare evidence strength across topics, identify a genuine uncertainty and propose a targeted new check without pretending it already occurred.

Evidence-map decisions

Use the digital choices or the matching paper page. One response mode is enough.

Use a real page, file or named card. Do not invent a locator for missing work.

Check

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON B · 2 MINUTES

Check one piece of evidence

Check one piece of evidence

Can another adult locate the evidence? Is it the pupil’s actual response, and is its date/origin honest?

Worked explanation · reveal after thinking

Accept specific claims supported by actual located evidence or clearly labelled new responses. DN1: Earth’s rotation changes whether a location faces sunlight. CL1: greenhouse gases do not stop all energy escaping. RR1 supports longer smooth travel only here. SH1 supports different disc/sphere outline patterns. Missing work remains “not found yet”; no automatic award claim.

Refine

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · LESSON B · 6 MINUTES

Improve one science explanation

Improve the science, not the amount of writing

Retain the first answer. Add a specific observation, repair a causal link, clarify the source or narrow an overclaim. Do not demand extra writing for its own sake.

Point, speak, sign, move a card, draw or write. One useful change is enough.

Answer: No. It is new evidence and must be labelled as such.

Knowledge organiser

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · Shared resource · Shared resource

Learning objective

I can locate or create honest science evidence, explain what it shows and improve one response after a focused check.

Key words

locator — where the evidence can be found

claim — what the evidence is used to support

provenance — where a record came from

revision — an improvement to a response

uncertain — not yet established by the available evidence

Remember

  • A supplied example is not a pupil’s earlier work.
  • “Not found yet” is an honest evidence-map entry.
  • Fresh work can show understanding today without being backdated.
  • An award or assessment judgement needs the relevant criteria and a teacher’s review.

Success looks like

  • Give a clear locator for an actual piece of evidence.
  • Connect a science claim to a relevant observation and a limit.
  • Label new evidence as new and keep a meaningful before/after response.

My claim is ___. My evidence is at ___. It supports the claim because ___. One limit is ___.

TA Brief

Current stage

Current stage:

Preparation and access

Use only authorised pupil records; do not display another learner’s personal work. Provide the neutral examples for anyone without earlier sheets. Accept speaking, pointing or an adult-scribed record in the pupil’s own words; keep response modes equivalent.

Scientific care

Do not fabricate, backdate or silently substitute missing pupil evidence. The supplied cards are neutral teaching examples; pupils may respond to them now, labelled as new work. Automated choices, downloaded files and word count do not certify understanding or an award.

Responsive feedback within teaching

The lesson teacher hears an optional request, explains what can change, tries it and checks the effect. Passing or asking privately is valid. No compulsory participation task or new pupil form. Do not infer assessment codes from a click, download or written box.

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · Lesson A · Supported

Name: ____________________

Four checks. Point, speak, sign, draw, write or direct an adult.

1. Findable evidence

Which is a useful locator: “somewhere” or “book page 6, table 1”?

Help: Point, choose or say. Another adult should be able to find it.

2. Missing work

Choose “not found yet” or “invent a page number”.

Help: Do not guess evidence.

3. New response

You explain a supplied card today. Is this new evidence or proof you wrote it last month?

Help: Point, choose or say. Separate today from an earlier record.

4. Relevant reason

Which explains day/night: rotation or a recycling label?

Help: Point, choose or say. Match the science to the claim.

Evidence cards

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · Shared resource · Shared resource

Read a clue, choose a group, then explain. Cut apart or point; no cutting is required.

Located table

A real file and table show three trials for each tested surface.

Today’s new answer

The response is labelled new and points to the supplied DN1 diagram.

Value with no unit

The record says 48 but does not identify the unit or measured quantity.

Claim only

The answer says “Earth rotates” but has not linked it to a light observation.

Invented old page

A page number was guessed because the earlier book is missing.

A click proves an award

A completed digital choice has not been judged against qualification criteria.

Answers · A · Standard

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · Lesson A · Standard

Four-question arrival

1. Findable evidence: Book page 6, table 1.

2. Missing work: Not found yet.

3. New response: New evidence.

4. Relevant reason: Rotation.

Two-check exit

1. Evidence map: Accept a genuine locator or clearly labelled new response; do not accept invented earlier evidence.

2. Explain the link: Accept a specific link, e.g. RR1 compares repeated travel distances for the two surfaces.

MADE BY MATT / GROW SCIENCE

Staff · feedback and access

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 7 · Shared resource · Shared resource

Audience and response

The lesson teacher is the named adult audience. Hear or read the pupil’s own science response. A click, downloaded file or completed box is not evidence that a request was heard.

Respond within the existing task

Offer reading help, fewer cards at once, clearer labels, an adult-directed model or additional thinking time. Say what can and cannot change, then check whether the adjustment helped.

No additional pupil artefact

A response can be spoken, pointed, signed, drawn or written. Do not require a separate Lundy record, signature or written conversion of an oral response.

An optional pupil-owned note such as “What I said, and what it changed” may be used in existing work. It is not a requirement. If scribing, keep the pupil’s own words; the adult is an audience, not a verifier.

Keep assessment honest

Use current school recording practice and unit criteria separately. This pack does not certify an award. Do not infer a policy code from automated checking or a download.
